scope: Static producer and detached-verifier CLI admission/resource audit against the proposed 218-segment Ethereum-SHA schedule; no mainnet block proof or benchmark

receiver_fix.problem: Detached rehydration used ArenaAllocator for replayed runner segments and staged proof-file loads, making per-segment free ineffective and retaining all 218 leaves' temporary allocations.
receiver_fix.change: runner.Source and one-at-a-time memory, execution, leaf and parent file loaders now use the bounded freeing host allocator; only borrowed metadata and at most 256 MiB of table proof bytes use the arena.

remaining_caps_and_risks: Producer and verifier each use a fixed 40 GiB tracked host budget. The full 218-segment producer peak has not been measured; a 16 GiB candidate-roster attempt exhausted its budget at segment 29, while later candidate probes with a larger budget continued. Do not infer 40 GiB suffices for all native proofs.
Recursive forest and outer preparation each have a 24 GiB scoped limit. The one-segment producer reached 14.09 GiB tracked and 14.24 GiB process RSS; the mainnet maximum leaf may be larger.

Each staged memory STARK has a 64 MiB serialized limit; execution and recursive files have a 256 MiB per-file limit. A real log20 memory instance measured 406342 bytes, but no largest mainnet execution/recursive proof size has been measured.

Bundle and recursion-policy JSON each have a 16 MiB limit; exact 218-segment serialized metadata size is not yet measured. The detached receiver retains table proof bytes under a separate 256 MiB aggregate cap.

Producer and verifier now report normalized process peak RSS and elapsed nanoseconds. The read-only candidate-roster CLI still reports tracked allocator peak only; wrap any mainnet proposal command with OS process RSS timing.
qualification_boundary: The 218-segment geometry and memory census are host-side admission evidence. Complete mainnet production and detached verification remain unproved.
